feedback: The user preferred the Claude original because its UX looked like Notion, the marketing page was cleaner like a SaaS company landing page, and the satire was funnier. The original and first attempt are withheld; this brief describes the quality target without providing their copy or implementation.
demo_requirements: Build an unmistakably Notion-like document workspace: a compact warm-gray page sidebar, plain breadcrumb and share/comments chrome, a page icon and a sans-serif document title, editable-looking blocks, an integrated database toolbar and a dense table with typed properties.

Use predominantly white and warm-gray surfaces with near-black text. Soft status colors encode actual database state. Avoid a blue SaaS skin, large serif app headings, framed dashboard panels, and a decorative wedding-themed sidebar.

Keep the request database as the main working surface. Search, status filters, table/board views, row side-peek, editable status, request counters, comments, new requests, AI summary, and the locked timeline block must work with consistent shared state.

Use clear controls and compact row density. At a 1440x900 desktop viewport, show at least six song records without scrolling the whole page. In narrow viewports use a small menu trigger and overlay drawer instead of stacking a tall sidebar above the document.

Support keyboard activation of rows, Escape to dismiss overlays, visible focus and labelled inputs. New requests must remain discoverable after filtering, and empty search states must provide a clear reset action.
landing_requirements: Design a restrained product-led SaaS landing page that credibly sells a wedding-DJ workspace. Favor clear hierarchy, confident typography, a quiet mostly neutral palette, one accent, a visible working-product preview and concise copy.

The marketing page can have a subtle wedding cue. Its main purpose is to sell the software; avoid heavily ornamental invitation styling, elaborate frames, large pale-blue color fields, excessive vertical gaps and a repeated card kit.
Use the supplied portraits with original testimonials. Keep pricing entitlement text specific enough to carry a joke. Hero and pricing calls to action must open a meaningful matching demo state.
writing_requirements: Find fresh, precise observations about the actual work of wedding DJs: conflicting requests, timing, venue constraints, duplicate demands, guest access and repeated set-list choices. Develop three distinct comic mechanisms rather than repeating generic family-politics language.

Keep the original named product and demo premise, including the immovable Cha Cha Slide. Write the hero, features, plans, testimonials, records and secondary UI text independently. Do not borrow lines from the baseline or the first Codex attempt.
